info.title: HidePages API
info.description:
Programmatic access to the HidePages platform: pages, campaigns, domains, funnel steps, A/B tests, conversion integrations and analytics — everything the panel does, over REST and JSON.

## Authenticating

Send an API key as the `X-API-Key` header. A key belongs to an account and works while that account holds an active or past-due subscription. Keys are issued in the panel or with the create-key endpoint, shown once, and stored only as a hash.

## What a caller can reach

A workspace is the dataset of its owner. Lists are scoped to the caller's active workspace, and a single resource is reachable when the caller owns the account it belongs to, or is a member of its workspace holding a sufficient level on that kind of resource — view to read, edit to write.

Asking for a resource the caller cannot reach answers **404, never 403** — a 403 would confirm that the id exists.

## Errors

Every failure answers an object with a single `error` member holding a code, a message, an optional field and a timestamp. Switch on the code; the message is for people and its wording may change. The field names the offending request field when the failure is about one. A 503 carries a `Retry-After` header.

## Lists

Collections answer a `data` array alongside a `pagination` object. Page numbers are 1-based and the page size is clamped to a maximum. Listing API keys is the one exception: it answers a bare array, because a caller holds only a handful of keys.

## Pages

Pages are authored in the current editor's content shape, and only that one: `settings.version` is `2`. Pages have a published row and a working draft. A PATCH writes the draft, and both a GET and the PATCH's own answer return the draft merged over the published row. Publishing promotes one to the other; until it runs visitors keep getting the published content. A publish reports `propagation`: whether every visitor-facing cache has the new version yet.

## Domains

A domain made here is the same as one made in the panel: the platform registers it, decides which edge serves it, and hands back the DNS records to create. Add it, create the records, verify.

## Analytics

The figures the dashboard shows, from the same store, per account, per campaign, per funnel step and per A/B test, plus the visit log. Never zeros in place of an error: a store that does not answer is a 503.

tags.description:
Traffic, connect rate, conversions and revenue — the same figures the dashboard shows, from the
same store. Read-only. Every date is `YYYY-MM-DD` and is interpreted in the account's timezone
(`users.timezone`, defaulting to America/Sao_Paulo), both ends inclusive.

Figures are scoped by **account**, not by workspace: events record the account that owns the
campaign. Without `campaignId` an endpoint reports on the owner of the caller's active
workspace, which for a staff key is the staff account itself — pass `campaignId` to read a
customer's numbers.

A `503 ANALYTICS_UNAVAILABLE` means the store did not answer; the figures are never replaced by
zeros. Answers are reused for a few seconds per identical question, so a value can lag a poll
by that much.

post.description:
Promotes the draft to the published row, which is what the edge serves. Repeatable.

Two things happen beyond the copy, so the published HTML is deliberately not byte-identical
to the draft:

1. Elements carrying `data-external-url` are wrapped in a real `<a href>` with
   `display:contents`. Tracking scripts that append an id look for `href`, and a `div`
   cannot carry one. The draft keeps the attribute, because the editor needs it.
2. Every campaign serving this page has its status recomputed. Publishing the last
   unpublished page is what moves a campaign from pending to ok. A campaign a billing
   job has blocked is left alone.

Publishing also evicts the page from every visitor-facing cache. When the platform has
a cache to report on, the response carries `propagation`: `complete` means visitors
get the new version now; `pending` (with a 207) means one cache has not confirmed yet,
the eviction is being retried on its own, and `retryAfterSeconds` bounds how long the
previous version may still be seen. Nothing needs redoing in either case.

409.description: The page has no draft to publish, or the draft has no name.

200.description: The page as published, with the external links rewritten. When the response carries `propagation`, its status is `complete`: every visitor-facing cache has the new version.

207.description: Published, but not every visitor-facing cache has acknowledged the new version yet. `propagation.status` is `pending` and `propagation.retryAfterSeconds` bounds how long the previous version may still be served; the eviction is retried without any further call. Nothing is lost and nothing needs redoing.

post.description:
The domain and every page referenced must belong to the **same workspace** as the campaign,
otherwise this answers 404: without that rule a caller could have their own hostname serving
another account's page.

`rules` is assembled rather than stored as sent, mirroring what the app does:

- `traffic-source` is required and must be one of `google`, `youtube`, `meta`, `tiktok`,
  `outbrain`, `taboola`, `newsbreak`, `mediago`, `mgid` — or omitted in favour of the
  Digistore24 upsell, marked by `campaign-mode: "upsell"` and
  `checkout-source: "digistore24"`. An absent source is refused because the edge would then
  skip the rule and serve the black page to any traffic.
- `device` is filtered to `mobile`/`desktop` and must end up non-empty. Empty is not "any
  device": the edge skips the rule when the list is empty.
- `suspicious-connection` is **forced on** for every source except `meta`, because the
  viewer requires it there. Sending `false` does not turn it off.
- The **gray surface is Meta-only**. `grayPageId`, `grayMirrorUrl`, `grayRedirectUrl` and
  `grayPageScripts` are cleared for any other source.
- Keys the platform does not know about are kept as sent.

Each surface is served one of three ways: a builder page (`*PageId`), a mirror of another
host's HTML (`*MirrorUrl`), or a redirect (`*RedirectUrl`). URLs are validated — a
scheme-less host is promoted to `https://`, and a host without a dot is refused.

`*PageScripts` are arrays of whole `<script>` tags, restricted to an allow-list of tracking
hosts and a set of known inline vendor snippets. Anything else is refused rather than
silently dropped, because these strings are written into a page real traffic sees.

`status`, `hideHash` and `integrationToken` are generated and cannot be supplied.

post.description:
A step answers on its own slug, in the **domain's** namespace — shared with campaigns and
with every other step on that domain, because the edge resolves a path segment against all
of them. Unlike a campaign's, a step's slug is lowercased before validation rather than
refused for its casing.

`type` is one of upsell, downsell or thankyou.

Pages must belong to the campaign's workspace **and be published** — stricter than a
